transcript.text: Bit of a weird one - my son put the microwave on for 10 minutes with nothing in it by accident. Now there's a horrible smell. Is it broken?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Running a microwave empty for 10 minutes is very hard on the magnetron (the part that generates heat) because there's nothing to absorb the energy. The 'horrible smell' is likely burnt dust from previous spills heating up, or potentially damage to internal components. Please do not use it again until you've checked this. With the microwave unplugged and cool, open the door and look at the inside walls, especially a small rectangular paper-like cover on the side (the waveguide cover). Is it intact and clean, or is it burnt/holey? Also check for any scorch marks or melted plastic inside.

It's only turned off at the switch, still plugged in, so I'll unplug it now. There was some smoke from the vents at the side when we stopped it, and the smell is fading but still there. Inside, I can see a brownish mark on the panel on the side wall. I'm not sure which bit the waveguide cover is, though. Is it safe to keep, or should I bin it?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
The combination of running it empty for 10 minutes and smoke coming from the vents suggests internal electrical damage, most likely to the magnetron (the component that generates heat) or a burnt waveguide cover. A brownish mark on the side panel is consistent with overheating in that area. Because this involves high-voltage components inside the casing, it is not safe for you to repair yourself, and attempting to use it again could be dangerous. Please arrange for a qualified engineer to inspect it; they will likely need to replace the damaged internal part.

candidates: Burnt dust or debris on internal components (high)
Melting plastic or food residue inside the cavity (medium)
Damage to the waveguide cover (mica sheet) (low)

plan: They asked: "Is it broken?" - answer that first.

Safety: a burning smell was reported. The fixed safety warning is shown separately, do not repeat it. It stays switched off and unplugged. Give the owner checks that are safe with it unplugged and cool and could show the cause (fluff or lint, a blocked or crushed vent, a jammed belt or brush bar, a food spill), as clear steps. Say plainly that if the smell was electrical (hot plastic or wiring), there was smoke or there are scorch marks, or the checks find no simple cause, it must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it. Never say or imply that it is safe to use again.
The fault they reported is: "horrible smell after running empty for 10 minutes". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
